title: telemetry-aggregation-pipeline-rearchitecture-retrospective-2025
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:

This retrospective documents the design, rollout, and outcomes of the Telemetry Aggregation Pipeline rearchitecture (internal codename: TARP). The project converted our previous per-service push model into a region-aware, event-driven aggregation layer to reduce cardinality, eliminate redundant ingestion, and align telemetry delivery with SLOs for metric/trace/trace-event availability across regions.

Background and motivation:

- Prior state: each service pushed metrics directly into region-local collectors. This caused noisy cardinality growth, duplicate events for multi-region services, wide variance in ingestion latency (P50=5s, P95=18s, P99=90s), and frequent alert flapping when cross-region clients hit inconsistent views.
- Goals: reduce ingest cost by 35% via deduplication + batching, stabilize metric delivery so 99.9% of important telemetry arrives within 60s, simplify downstream dashboards by providing a single canonical time-series per logical entity, and provide a safe migration path with rollbacks.

High-level architecture changes made:

- Introduced three new components: ingest-router (region-aware front door), event-aggregator (de-duplicate + continuous-batch), and canonical-sharder (assigns logical entity -> canonical shard).
- Kept existing telemetry-collector as a thin adapter so clients required minimal change (SDK version 2.1.0).
- Added per-tenant sampling policies + prefix-based metric normalization rules (config stored in config-service /telemetry/policies).

Key timeline (major milestones):

1) 2024-07-02: Design review (architecture ADR-2024-11-TARP) approved.
2) 2024-08-10: Prototype of event-aggregator + local synthetic load tests (k8s namespaces: tarp-dev).
3) 2024-09-15: Canary deploy to us-west-2 (10% of traffic for non-critical namespaces).
4) 2024-10-07: Expanded canary to multi-region (us-west-2 + eu-central-1) with feature flag gating.
5) 2024-10-28: Production rollout completed for non-enterprise tenants.
6) 2024-11-12: Enterprise tenant phased rollouts started with Dedicated-only paths.
7) 2024-12-01: Full production: cross-region dedupe and canonical metrics enabled globally.

Quantitative outcomes (pre vs post):

| Metric | Baseline (Aug 2024) | After rollout (Dec 2024) | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Ingest cost (monthly) | $320,000 | $198,000 | -38% |
| Cardinality (unique metrics/day) | 9.4M | 5.6M | -40% |
| Metric delivery P95 (s) | 18 | 9 | -50% |
| Missing metric alerts per week (global) | 24 | 6 | -75% |
| Dashboard mismatch incidents (per quarter) | 7 | 1 | -86% |

What went well:

- SDK compatibility strategy: allowing telemetry-collector as thin adapter reduced required client changes to environment variables (SDK upgrade adoption: 88% within 6 weeks).
- Canary phasing by tenant-type (non-critical -> multi-region -> enterprise) avoided large-scale regressions and allowed targeted rollback for a handful of enterprise integrations with custom scraping behavior.
- Operator tooling: we developed a fast verification dashboard that correlated ingest rates, dedupe counts, and canonical shard reassignments that was invaluable during rollout.
- Cost and SLO improvements measured above (notable cost savings were recognized in finance runbook and monthly invoices).

What didn't go well / Root causes:

- Unexpected dedupe churn: During the multi-region canary, the canonical-sharder reassigned ~0.7% of entities more than once due to clock skew and inconsistent entity tags. Root cause: incomplete tag normalization rules and a missing TTL on pre-shard claims.
- Migration warnings overload: Operators experienced alert storms from validation rules that assumed pre-rollout cardinality. Root cause: alert thresholds were not parameterized per-phase and used absolute counts rather than rate-of-change.
- Enterprise scraping edge cases: Several enterprise customers used custom scraping endpoints that emitted ephemeral labels leading to high churn. Root cause: lack of integration tests that represent customer scraping diversity.

Mitigations taken during rollout:

- Fast patch: added a 60s soft-claim TTL and strengthened namespace->entity tag normalization in canonical-sharder (rollout 2024-10-12).
- Alert tuning: implemented phased alert multipliers (factor=0.5 during canary) and switched to rate-based derivations for validation alarms.
- Enterprise remediation: created an enterprise-scrape-compatibility guide and a compatibility testing harness (tarp-enterprise-testkit) for solutions engineers.

Operator runbook (short version) — for incidents where metric delivery degradation is detected:

1) Verify scope: open the TARP verification dashboard and check ingest-router throughput, aggregator dedupe-rate, and canonical-sharder reassignment rate. Note region(s) and tenants impacted.
2) If dedupe-rate spikes > 5x baseline or shard reassignments > 1%/5m, flip feature flag: tarp-aggregation = disabled for impacted region.
3) If ingestion falls to < 70% of baseline: scale ingest-router replicas (kubectl -n telemetry scale deploy/ingest-router --replicas=<n>) and check backpressure metrics on Kafka topic tarp-events.
4) For enterprise tenants reporting missing metrics, enable per-tenant bypass (config-service /telemetry/skip-aggregation/<tenant-id>) and notify solutions engineering.
5) After stabilization, run a backfill job (backfill-aggregates --start=<iso> --end=<iso>) and verify canonical counts match expected totals.

Rollback checklist (if a full rollback is required):

- Notify stakeholders (oncall, product, solutions engineering, customer success).
- Flip tarp-global-mode = passive in feature-flagging service.
- Recreate per-region direct-forwarding routes by toggling ingest-router -> collector route to direct.
- Ensure telemetry-collector adapters are set to pre-aggregation mode (env TELEMETRY_ADAPTER_MODE=legacy).
- Monitor for 2x ingress and potential cost surge; request temporary budget approval from finance if expected.

Lessons learned and recommended standards to adopt company-wide:

- Phased alerting: alerts that run during rollout must be parameterized by phase (canary / phased-rollout / GA) and derive thresholds via both absolute and rate-of-change signals.
- Claim/lease semantics: any component that 'claims' canonical ownership must use soft TTLs and Versioned-Claims to avoid oscillation during partial network partitions.
- Tenant integration testing: expand integration test matrix in CI to include enterprise scrape diversity (custom labels, ephemeral endpoints, multi-scrape intervals).
- Cost telemetry: shipping monthly cost deltas to finance early enables quicker business sign-off and reduces surprise escalations.
- Operator dashboards: create a single verification dashboard per major rollout that shows pre/post deltas and a small checklist for safe promotion.

Action items (owners and dates):

- [P0] Tag normalization rulesheet (owner: Priya Kapoor) — due 2025-02-01.
- [P0] Implement Versioned-Claims for canonical-sharder (owner: Carlos Mendes) — due 2025-03-01.
- [P1] Add enterprise-testkit to CI (owner: Evan Liu) — due 2025-02-15.
- [P1] Alert parameterization library (owner: Diego Santos) — due 2025-01-30.
- [P2] Finance integration for monthly cost deltas (owner: Finance-API team) — due 2025-04-01.

Appendix: Useful commands and links:

- Quick verification dashboard: /dashboards/tarp/verification (internal link)
- Canary feature flag path: /flags/tarp-aggregation (use rollout tags: canary,multi-region,enterprise,ga)
- Backfill job: ./ops/backfill-aggregates --help
- Test clusters: tarp-dev (k8s), tarp-staging (k8s), tarp-prod (k8s)
- Relevant ADR: ADR-2024-11-TARP (link internal)

Conclusion:

The Telemetry Aggregation Pipeline rearchitecture delivered substantial cost and SLO improvements while revealing important operational and testing gaps—particularly around claim semantics and enterprise scraping diversity. The mitigations and action items above are prioritized to reduce future migration risk and to codify safe rollout practices for future platform-wide changes.
